directAnswer: A CPU may not work due to improper installation, power supply issues, or hardware failures.
summary: Identifying why a CPU is not functioning can involve checking connections, power supply, and hardware compatibility.

sections.heading: Installation Issues
sections.body: Ensure the CPU is correctly seated in the socket and that the locking mechanism is properly engaged. Check that thermal paste is applied correctly and the cooler is securely attached.

sections.heading: Power Supply Check
sections.body: Verify that the power supply unit (PSU) is functioning and providing adequate power to the motherboard and CPU. Check all power connectors, especially the 4-pin or 8-pin CPU power connector.

sections.heading: Hardware Failures
sections.body: Test the CPU in another compatible motherboard if possible, or try a different CPU in the current motherboard to rule out hardware failures.

steps.title: Check CPU Installation
steps.detail: Power down the PC, unplug it, and remove the side panel. Carefully check that the CPU is seated properly in the socket.

steps.title: Inspect Power Connections
steps.detail: Ensure that all power connectors, especially the CPU power connector, are securely connected to the motherboard.

steps.title: Test with Minimal Configuration
steps.detail: Remove all non-essential hardware and boot the system with only the CPU, one stick of RAM, and the power supply connected.

faqs.question: What should I do if the CPU fan is not spinning?
faqs.answer: Check the power connections to the fan and ensure the fan is not obstructed. If it still doesn't spin, the fan may be faulty.

faqs.question: How can I tell if my CPU is dead?
faqs.answer: If the system shows no signs of life (no lights, no fan movement) after checking all connections, the CPU may be dead, but testing in another motherboard is recommended.

faqs.question: Can a faulty power supply affect CPU performance?
faqs.answer: Yes, an inadequate or failing power supply can lead to unstable power delivery, which may cause the CPU to malfunction or not boot.

caveats: Always ensure you are grounded to prevent static damage when handling computer components.
